title: Correctness of the enumerator run
statement: Let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $o_0,o_1$ be Boolean-valued oracles such that, for every Boolean word $x$ and natural number $j$, $o_0(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(j)\rangle)$ is true exactly when $j<|f(x)|$, and $o_1(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(j)\rangle)$ equals the $j$-th bit of $f(x)$, defaulting to false when absent. If $|f(x)|\le F$ and $|\operatorname{bits}(j+1)|\le W$ for every $j<|f(x)|$, then the enumerator, started in its initial configuration on $x$, reaches after some finite number $N$ of steps a halted configuration whose output is $f(x)$ and whose work-tape head is at position zero. Every configuration at a time strictly less than $N$ has shape bounded by $F$ and $W$.
hypotheses_covered: The length oracle correctly tests whether an index is below the output length
The bit oracle returns the output bit, defaulting to false when absent
The output length is at most $F$
For every index below the output length, the bit length of its successor is at most $W$
